mainTopic: Separating תרומה on יום טוב, אביי's two versions about when legume bundles become טבל, and a לוי who took מעשר ראשון early.
overview: The גמרא first resolves a contradiction about separating תרומה on יום טוב. It suggests that the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows רבי, who disagree about grain stalks brought in to be husked. Because even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה has a case where the obligation begins on יום טוב, the גמרא concludes instead that the משנה's ban covers only the usual case of תרומה. אביי then limits the dispute to grain stalks and says everyone agrees that legume bundles are טבל. An attempt to prove this from a ruling about bundles of תלתן fails, because תלתן was mentioned for a different lesson: you separate based on the seeds, not the flavorful stalks. In a second version, אביי says everyone agrees legume bundles are not טבל. The תלתן ruling is explained as referring to produce that is טבל only for תרומת מעשר, following ריש לקיש's rule about a לוי who took מעשר ראשון early. רבא explains that the required pounding is a penalty on that לוי. A ברייתא supports this, and its reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two sources, two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction between the ברייתא and the משנה by assigning them to two different authorities: רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This source (the ברייתא) follows רבי. That source (the משנה) follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from the end of the previous daf. It says the ברייתא and the משנה simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, grain stalks can become obligated in תרומה before they are fully processed, so the obligation could begin on יום טוב itself. In that case one may separate on יום טוב, which is the ברייתא's case. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, there is no such case, so the משנה can say flatly that תרומה is never separated on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: This one (pointing to one of two sources)
רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה
A תנא, son of רבי יהודה
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הא רבי' as a statement of halacha. It is a label saying which source goes with which opinion: the first 'הא' is the ברייתא and the second 'הא' is the משנה.

phrases.english: This (the ברייתא) is according to Rabbi;
phrases.notes: רבי allows a case where the obligation begins on יום טוב.

phrases.english: that (the משנה) is according to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: He leaves no such case, so the משנה can be absolute.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַבִּי, הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised on the previous daf between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the conflicting sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to give opposite rulings about separating תרומה on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a מחלוקת between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about when grain stalks become obligated.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute about grain stalks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא proving that רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree about stalks brought in to be husked and eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: If someone brought stalks into his house in order to make dough from them, he may snack on them and is exempt. If he brought them in to husk them and eat the kernels, רבי obligates him and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה really do argue about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain normally becomes obligated only when its processing is finished. If the stalks were brought in to make dough, they are far from finished, so everyone agrees a casual snack is exempt. If they were brought in to be husked and eaten as kernels, רבי says bringing them inside for that purpose already makes them obligated. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says they are still exempt, so for him this obligation never starts in a way that could happen on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Stalks or ears of grain
Dough
Casually, as a snack (not a set meal)
To rub them into husked kernels
Obligates / exempts

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the factual basis for step 1's answer. Without a known מחלוקת, the גמרא could not assign the משנה and the ברייתא to different opinions.

phrases.english: As it is taught: If one brought in stalks of grain
in order to make dough from them,
phrases.notes: His plan requires much more processing, so the grain is not yet 'finished.'

phrases.english: he may eat from them as a snack, and is exempt.
If he brought them in to rub them into kernels,
phrases.notes: His plan is to eat them almost as they are.

phrases.english: Rabbi obligates him (to separate first),
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הִכְנִיס שִׁבֳּלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵהֶן עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the מחלוקת used in the answer of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree about whether stalks brought in to be husked become obligated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about stalks brought into the house for dough versus for husking.

steps.title: Even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה has a case where the obligation begins on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 1: even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the obligation can begin on יום טוב, so the משנה cannot follow him and be absolute.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה you can find such a case: for example, he brought in stalks to make dough from them, and then on יום טוב he changed his mind and decided to husk them. They become טבל on that very day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. It shows that even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה has a case where produce first becomes obligated on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stalks brought into the house for dough are already set up to become obligated once their processing is complete. When the owner decides on יום טוב to eat them as husked kernels, that decision completes their processing, so they become טבל right then, on יום טוב. That is exactly the ברייתא's case, so assigning the משנה to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not make its absolute rule work.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (such a case)
And he reconsidered or changed his mind
It becomes טבל (untithed, forbidden until separated)
On that very day

steps.confusionAlert: Note the difference from step 2. There, the stalks were brought in from the start to be husked. Here, they were brought in for dough and the plan changed on יום טוב. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees that this second case becomes obligated.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
you can also find it (such a case):
for example, where he brought in stalks
to make dough from them,
and on יום טוב he changed his mind about them, deciding to husk them,
so it becomes טבל on that very day!
phrases.notes: The obligation begins on יום טוב, so separating could not have been done the day before.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's absolute ban follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even he agrees that stalks brought in for dough become טבל on יום טוב if the owner then decides to husk them, so for him too the obligation can arise on יום טוב.

steps.title: The משנה means the usual, majority case of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the answer of step 1 and explains that the משנה's ban refers only to the common case, while unusual cases where the obligation begins on יום טוב are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the 'תרומה' that the משנה forbids? It is the majority of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the original contradiction. The משנה was speaking only about the normal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In most cases, grain is already finished and obligated before יום טוב (for example, grain threshed and piled on ערב יום טוב). That תרומה should have been separated beforehand, so it may not be separated on יום טוב. The unusual case, where the obligation first begins on יום טוב, is permitted, as the ברייתא says. So the two sources no longer contradict each other, and this holds according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the previous answer and offering a new one)
What is (the meaning of)
Most תרומה, meaning the common, typical case

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ban on separating תרומה on יום טוב covers the normal case, where produce was already obligated before יום טוב. If the obligation first begins on יום טוב itself, separating is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer replaces the 'two תנאים' approach. The משנה's general rule now sits alongside a narrow exception, instead of the sources being split between disputing opinions.

phrases.english: Rather: what is the 'תרומה' (of the משנה)?
Most תרומה (the typical case).
phrases.notes: This is grain that was already obligated before יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 1, which was refuted in step 3, with a new reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the משנה's wording to the typical case (אוקימתא of the term).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'תרומה' meant all תרומה without exception, which forced it to follow one specific תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תרומה' in the משנה means the majority case, produce already obligated before יום טוב. Exceptional cases where the obligation begins on יום טוב are permitted.

steps.title: אביי limits the dispute to grain stalks
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the מחלוקת between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is only about שבלין. With קטניות, everyone agrees the bundles are טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The argument is only about stalks of grain. But with legumes, everyone agrees that the bundles are already untithed produce (טבל).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a new statement that narrows the argument we saw earlier between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that stalks brought in to be husked are not yet טבל. אביי says this leniency applies only to grain. Legumes are normally brought home in bundles, so being bundled is their finished stage. Even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees they are already טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument or dispute
Stalks or ears of grain
Legumes (beans, lentils and similar)
Everyone agrees
Bundles
Is טבל: produce whose תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been taken, so it may not be eaten

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The dispute is about stalks of grain.
phrases.notes: The argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה from step 2.

phrases.english: But with legumes —
everyone agrees the bundles are untithed produce (טבל).
phrases.notes: Legumes are usually stored in bundles, so the bundle is their finished form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the מחלוקת that was proven in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is limited to שבלין. With קטניות, everyone agrees bundles are טבל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's leniency depends on the normal way each crop is processed, not on a blanket rule.

steps.title: A possible support from bundles of fenugreek
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ruling about bundles of תלתן supports אביי. It seems to follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, yet it treats legume bundles as טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a source supports him? 'Someone who has bundles of fenugreek that are untithed may pound them. He calculates how many seeds are in them and separates תרומה based on the seeds, not on the stalks.' Isn't this the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said: there (grain stalks) it is not טבל, but here (legume bundles) it is טבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring a proof for אביי from a ruling about bundles of תלתן (fenugreek, a kind of legume).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling treats the bundles of תלתן as already טבל, since it calls them טבל and tells him to separate from the seeds. If this follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, then he agrees that legume bundles are טבל even though grain stalks are not. That is exactly what אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
Fenugreek, a kind of legume
Pounds, beats out the seeds
Literally 'wood'; here the stalks of the plant
Is it not so that…? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן שֶׁל טֶבֶל —
phrases.english: One who had bundles of untithed fenugreek —
he may pound them,
and calculate how much seed is in them,
and separate תרומה based on the seeds,
but he does not separate based on the stalks.
Is it not —
following Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: there (grain stalks) it is not טבל,
but here (legume bundles) it is טבל!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support אביי's statement from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees legume bundles are טבל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling about bundles of תלתן of טבל, read as following רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: The ruling may follow רבי instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ruling about תלתן could follow רבי, who holds that even grain stalks are טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by saying the ruling about תלתן might follow רבי, not רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that even stalks brought in for husking are טבל. Of course he agrees that bundles of תלתן are טבל. So the ruling tells us nothing about what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה thinks about legumes, and the support for אביי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggestion)
רבי יהודה הנשיא
It is (following the view of…)

phrases.english: No, it follows Rebbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the attribution of the תלתן ruling to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. אביי's statement itself is not attacked.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling could just as easily follow רבי, so it cannot show what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds.

steps.title: If it follows רבי, why mention fenugreek?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection: if the ruling follows רבי, why did it pick תלתן when the same law applies even to grain stalks?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי, why talk specifically about fenugreek? Even grain stalks would be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 7 by asking why the ruling chose תלתן as its example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, even grain stalks are טבל. If the ruling followed רבי, it should have taught the bigger point with grain stalks. Choosing תלתן seems to show the author draws a line between grain and legumes, which is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: If
Why specifically this case?
Even … as well

phrases.english: If it follows Rebbi,
why specifically fenugreek?
Even grain stalks would be the same!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי הִיא, מַאי אִירְיָא תִּלְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 7 and tries to bring back the proof of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the תלתן ruling follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי, grain stalks are also טבל. A ruling that follows רבי would not limit itself to the narrower example of תלתן.

steps.title: The same question applies to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'why fenugreek?' question works just as well against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He too should have taught about legumes in general. So the choice of תלתן proves nothing, and the ruling can still follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what then? That it follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה? Then let it teach us about other kinds of legumes, and fenugreek all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rejection by showing that the 'why fenugreek?' question bothers both opinions equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling followed רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, it should have taught the general rule about all legumes, and we would know fenugreek automatically. Neither view explains why תלתן was chosen. So the ruling must have its own reason for mentioning תלתן: the point about separating from the seeds and not the stalks. This means the choice of example cannot tell us who wrote it, and the proof for אביי stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what [would you say]? Introduces a counter-question
Let it teach us
Other kinds of
All the more so

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says everyone agrees legume bundles are טבל. The attempt to prove this from the ruling about תלתן fails, because that ruling could follow רבי. The question 'why fenugreek?' does not decide the matter, since it applies to both opinions.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not prove that the ruling follows רבי. It only shows that the 'why fenugreek?' question cannot decide the author, so the proof for אביי is left unproven. It is not disproven either.

phrases.english: Rather, what [would you say]?
That it follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?
Then let it teach us other kinds of legumes,
and all the more so fenugreek.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels the challenge of step 8 by showing it applies equally to the other opinion, so the rejection in step 7 stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the question applies to both sides equally (a counter-question).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Choosing תלתן suggests the ruling follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, which would support אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Choosing תלתן is unexplained under either opinion. The ruling has its own reason for using תלתן, so it cannot show who wrote it, and the proof for אביי fails.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling about תלתן does not prove אביי's statement. His statement remains standing, without support from this source.

steps.title: The real reason the ruling mentions fenugreek
steps.stepSummary: The ruling chose תלתן because its stalk tastes like its seeds. Without the ruling, we might have thought you must also separate תרומה based on the stalks. The ruling teaches that you do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case of fenugreek was needed for its own lesson. You might have thought: since the taste of fenugreek's stalk and its seeds is the same, one should also separate תרומה based on the stalk. So the teaching tells us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason why the ruling mentions תלתן. This finally answers the 'why fenugreek?' question from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תלתן has a special feature: its stalks add flavor just like its seeds. So someone might think the stalks count as food for תרומה purposes. The ruling picks תלתן to teach that you separate only based on the seeds. This means the choice of תלתן has nothing to do with the רבי / רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה debate, so it cannot prove אביי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Fenugreek, a legume whose stalks also have flavor
It was needed for him (the teaching had a specific reason to mention it)
It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken assumption)
Its stalk ('wood') and its fruit (seeds)
It teaches us (the new lesson)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling mentions תלתן to teach that you separate תרומה only based on the seeds, not the flavorful stalks. So the ruling proves nothing about אביי's rule.

phrases.english: Rather, fenugreek was needed for him [for its own reason].
It would have entered your mind to say:
Since the taste of its stalk and its fruit is the same,
one should also separate based on its stalk,
phrases.notes: That is, include the stalks when calculating how much תרומה to give.

phrases.english: so it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 9 showed that the 'why fenugreek?' question works against both opinions. This step gives the actual reason fenugreek was chosen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a specific case was chosen (a separate חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since fenugreek's stalk is as flavorful as its seeds, one might include the stalks when separating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: You separate only based on the seeds. That is the lesson, so the choice of תלתן says nothing about who the ruling follows.

steps.title: Second version of אביי's rule: legume bundles are not טבל
steps.stepSummary: Some report אביי's rule the opposite way: the מחלוקת is about grain stalks, but with קטניות everyone agrees the bundles are NOT טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that אביי said: the dispute is about grain stalks. But with legumes, everyone agrees that the bundles are not טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of אביי's statement that reaches the opposite conclusion about legume bundles. This sets up a new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 5), everyone agreed legume bundles ARE טבל. In this version, everyone agrees they are NOT טבל, because legumes are not considered finished while still in bundles. The debate between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה stays limited to grain stalks in both versions.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces a different version of a statement)
Bundles
They are not טבל (they do not create the obligation to tithe)
Legumes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 5. Both versions limit the מחלוקת to grain stalks. The difference is only about legumes: in version one they ARE טבל, and in this version they are NOT.

phrases.english: Some say:
Abaye said: the dispute is about [grain] stalks,
but with legumes, everyone agrees
the bundles are not untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first version's proof discussion, the גמרא presents an alternate version of אביי's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about grain stalks. With legumes, everyone agrees bundles are not טבל.

steps.title: Challenge from the fenugreek bundles ruling
steps.stepSummary: A ruling says bundles of תלתן can be טבל, and you separate based on the seeds. That seems to be ordinary טבל of תרומה, which contradicts the second version of אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: someone who had bundles of fenugreek that were טבל may pound them, figure out how much seed is in them, and separate based on the seeds, but not based on the stalks. Isn't this talking about produce that is טבל for regular תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version of אביי's rule using the same ruling about fenugreek bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תלתן is a legume, and the ruling calls its bundles 'טבל'. The natural reading is that they need regular תרומה, so legume bundles DO create the obligation. That directly contradicts 'everyone agrees legume bundles are not טבל.'

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (introduces a source that contradicts a statement)
Pounds / threshes
Calculates
Is it not? (introduces the challenger's assumed reading)
Produce that is טבל because regular תרומה has not yet been taken

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן שֶׁל טֶבֶל
phrases.english: One who had bundles of fenugreek that were untithed
may pound [them],
and calculate how much seed is in them,
and separate based on the seed,
but he does not separate based on the stalk.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, טֶבֶל טָבוּל שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה!
phrases.english: Is it not [talking about] produce that is untithed with regard to תרומה?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן שֶׁל טֶבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version of אביי's rule from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of אביי's rule: everyone agrees legume bundles are not טבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling calls fenugreek (legume) bundles 'טבל', which seems to mean they need regular תרומה. So legume bundles do create the obligation.

steps.title: The ruling means טבל only for תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is not about regular תרומה. It is about produce that is טבל only because its תרומת מעשר has not yet been separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about produce that is טבל only with regard to תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ruling as a different kind of טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are layers of טבל. Produce can be טבל because regular תרומה was not taken, or because the לוי has not yet taken תרומת מעשר from his tithe. The answer says the bundles here are only the second kind. So legume bundles can still be free from the regular obligation, and אביי's second version survives.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth that the לוי must give a כהן from the tithe he received

steps.confusionAlert: 'טבל' does not always mean the same thing. Here it means only that תרומת מעשר is still missing, not regular תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, טֶבֶל טָבוּל שֶׁל תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: No, [it is] produce that is untithed with regard to תרומת מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, טֶבֶל טָבוּל שֶׁל תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (a different kind of טבל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bundles are טבל for regular תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bundles are טבל only for תרומת מעשר, so they say nothing about the regular obligation for legume bundles.

steps.title: Source for how this case happens: ריש לקיש on early first tithe
steps.stepSummary: The answer follows the statement of רבי אבהו in the name of ריש לקיש about a לוי who took מעשר ראשון early, while the grain was still in stalks. Step 15 completes the statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows what רבי אבהו said in the name of ריש לקיש. For רבי אבהו said in the name of ריש לקיש: First tithe that was taken early, while the grain was still in stalks...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a source that explains how produce can be טבל only for תרומת מעשר. The quote finishes in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, regular תרומה is taken first, and only then מעשר ראשון. If a לוי takes his tithe early, while the grain is still in stalks, a special situation arises. The tithe he holds may still need תרומת מעשר even though the regular obligation does not apply to it. This explains the case from step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to the לוי
That he took early (before its normal order)
And this follows [the view of] רבי...

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the answer in step 13 can be real: a legume bundle can be 'טבל' for תרומת מעשר without being טבל for regular תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: And [this is] in line with what Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
First tithe that [the לוי] took early, while still in the stalks,
phrases.notes: The statement is completed in step 15.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind step 13's answer, showing how a case of טבל only for תרומת מעשר arises.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a לוי takes מעשר ראשון early while the grain is in stalks (the ruling is completed in step 15).

steps.title: The name 'מעשר' makes the produce טבל for תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's statement ends: when a לוי took מעשר ראשון while the grain was still in stalks, calling it מעשר ראשון is enough to make it טבל for תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its name, the fact that it is called מעשר, makes it טבל with regard to תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the statement of ריש לקיש that began earlier. Once produce is called מעשר ראשון, it becomes forbidden as טבל until its תרומת מעשר is separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, produce becomes טבל only after its processing is finished, for example after the grain is threshed and piled. Here, ריש לקיש says the name 'מעשר' alone creates the obligation of תרומת מעשר, even while the grain is still in stalks. This explains how the תלתן bundles in Step 12 can be טבל: they are טבל for תרומת מעשר, not for regular תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its name, meaning the fact that it has been designated as מעשר
Makes it טבל, so it is forbidden to eat until the required gift is separated
The tenth of his tithe that a לוי must give to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source behind the answer in Step 13. It shows a case where a kind of תרומה applies even before the produce is fully processed.

phrases.english: Its name makes it טבל
phrases.notes: Simply being designated as מעשר creates the obligation.

phrases.english: with regard to תרומת מעשר.
phrases.notes: Only for תרומת מעשר, not for regular תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement of ריש לקיש that was introduced in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once produce is designated as מעשר ראשון, even while it is still in stalks, it becomes טבל for תרומת מעשר.

steps.title: Why must the לוי pound the stalks?
steps.stepSummary: If the stalks are already טבל for תרומת מעשר, why does the ruling require pounding them? The לוי could simply give the כהן stalks, just as he received stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need pounding? Let him say to the כהן: 'Just as they gave to me, so I am giving to you!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling about תלתן, which says the stalks must be pounded first. It asks why the לוי cannot simply give the כהן unprocessed stalks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in Step 12 said one pounds the תלתן bundles, figures out how much seed is inside, and separates based on the seeds. If the obligation already started at the stalk stage, it seems fair for the לוי to give stalks. He received stalks, so why should he have to give something better?

keyTerms.meaning: He pounds, meaning he beats the stalks to get the seeds out
Why do I need it? This is a standard way of asking why something is necessary
Let him say to him

phrases.english: Why do I need pounding?
phrases.notes: This refers to the pounding mentioned in the תלתן ruling.

phrases.english: Let him (the לוי) say to him (the כהן):
Just as they gave to me,
so I am giving to you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses ריש לקיש's rule to question the pounding requirement in the תלתן ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement in the תלתן ruling to pound the bundles before separating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the obligation started at the stalk stage, the לוי should be allowed to give stalks, which is the same form in which he received the produce.

steps.title: The pounding is a penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that pounding is a קנס. Because the לוי took his share too early, the חכמים made him process it before giving the כהן his portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. By strict law the לוי could give stalks, but the חכמים penalized him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוי did something improper. He took his מעשר before the כהן's תרומה גדולה was separated, which cheated the כהן. As a penalty, he must process the produce and give the כהן a finished product.

keyTerms.meaning: A penalty imposed by the חכמים
An important אמורא who answers the question here

steps.confusionAlert: The pounding is not required by the basic law. By strict law, the לוי's claim ('just as they gave me') would be correct. The pounding is required only as a penalty.

phrases.english: רבא said: It is a penalty.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic penalty, not the basic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the obligation started with stalks, the לוי may give stalks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים penalized the לוי for taking his share early, so he must process the produce first.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: the לוי must process the produce first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a לוי who was given stalks, grapes, or olives as מעשר must turn them into grain, wine, or oil, and only then separate תרומת מעשר for the כהן. The reason starts with a comparison to תרומה גדולה and continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: A לוי who was given stalks as his tithes makes them into a threshed pile. If given grapes, he makes them into wine. If given olives, he makes them into oil. Then he separates תרומת מעשר from them and gives it to the כהן. For just as תרומה גדולה is not taken...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבא: the לוי must finish processing the produce before giving תרומת מעשר. The ברייתא starts giving its reason, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three kinds of produce (grain, grapes, olives). In every case, the לוי must bring the produce to its finished form first. It begins to explain this by comparing it to תרומה גדולה, which is not separated from unprocessed produce. The rest of the comparison comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also taught in a ברייתא, a phrase that introduces support
Stalks of grain
A threshing floor, or a threshed and piled grain heap
The main תרומה that the owner gives to the כהן

phrases.english: It is also taught this way (in a baraita):
A Levite who was given
stalks as his tithes —
makes them into a threshed pile,
phrases.notes: He threshes them in the usual way.

phrases.english: grapes — he makes them into wine,
olives — he makes them into oil,
and separates תרומת מעשר for them,
and gives them to the priest.
For just as תרומה גדולה
is not taken
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רבא's answer in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the לוי must process the produce before separating תרומת מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a לוי given stalks, grapes, or olives as his tithes.
